pr_title: *: table partition dynamic prune mode with Physical Table ID from unistore
pr_body:

### What problem does this PR solve?
<!--

Please create an issue first to describe the problem.

There MUST be one line starting with "Issue Number:  " and 
linking the relevant issues via the "close" or "ref".

For more info, check https://pingcap.github.io/tidb-dev-guide/contribute-to-tidb/contribute-code.html#referring-to-an-issue.

-->

Issue Number: close #29851

Problem Summary:

### What is changed and how it works?

The current issue with dynamic prune mode is that it uses a single TableReader which loses context which partition (physical table id) the different rows comes from, which is needed for SelectLock (SELECT FOR UPDATE) and comparison with the Transaction buffer.

By adding a virtual column with ExtraPhysTblID the engine can extract the physical table ID from the KV key that is read and append it to the row/chunk data.

issue_context.title: Invalid keys may get locked
comments:
From the debug log added in https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/28060.

[executor.go:957] ["[for debug] the physicalID or handle value is unexpected"] [conn=875] [ts=427743752351907842] [id=4568] [physicalID=0] [handle=10] [sql="/* tp-test:q:1631712899.f924863c-d083-4c81-913d-4b4618deffb1:69 */ select  * from t1 join t2 on t1.c_int = t2.c_int and t1.c_enum <= t2.c_enum for update"] [tblIDs="[4568,4487]"] [partTblLen=2] [tblID2PIDColIdxMapKeys="[4487,4568]"] [tblid2ColIdxMapVals="[8,16]"]

Seems the calculation for the physical id is unexpected, possibly  the `tblID2PIDColumnIndex` is set incorrectly.

@tiancaiamao 
PTAL

Caused by https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/26373 and related to https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/28292

When partition table need to handle lock(write the lock key), it add an extra partition ID column to the chunk. 
The bug is, the write operation does not recognize the extra partition ID column and write it back to the TiKV.

I find the root cause and will file a PR to fix.

`select * from t1 left join t2 on t1.c_int = t2.c_int for update;`

The join right side is NULL, added by the left join.
So there is no physical ID column... and we get the physical ID as 0, and construct the wrong key.

review_comments:
Logically, are `ExtraPhysTblID` and `ExtraPidColID` always the same (since `PartitionID` is just another name of the physical table ID of the corresponding partition)? While in implementation, they have different implementations.
Do I understand it correctly? If it is, could we remove `ExtraPidColID` in the future?

They will return the same information, but will be read from different sources, `ExtraPhysTblID` extracts the table id from the key (which is in the key-prefix for both table and index data) while `ExtraPidColID` is a normal column stored in a global index (with the logical table id in the key-prefix of the index key).

I think we should be able to remove the `ExtraPidColID` from TiKV and treat it as a hidden column in TiDB, which will only be used in the case of global index, but I think we can still use the dedicated `ExtraPidColID` for partition id/physical table id as a hidden column.

In theory we could extend the global index implementation to support partitioned indexes with different partitioning from the table, then we would need to use both `ExtraPhysTblID` for which index partition the row was read, and `ExtraPidColID` for which table partition the rowID/handle/PK belongs to.
OK, got it.
How about breaking the loop early when `us.columns[i].ID > 0`?

You mean relying on HandlerID, ExtraPIDColumn and ExtraPhysTblColID is always last?
Sure, but since this is in the `Open` function I think the overhead can be neglected, so I rather have it more generic, in case there will be changes that breaks the assumption of order of the requested columns.
What will happen if the column is in `tblID2PhysTblIDColIdx` but not found in `e.Schema().Columns`?
For example, the column is pruned, so it's not in `e.Schema().Columns`

Could you help me finding such test case?
To me the column would be added in `buildSelectLock` (by calling `setExtraPhysTblIDColsOnDataSource` / `AddExtraPhysTblIDColumn`) and then pruned by `(p *LogicalLock) PruneColumns` which would move the column pruning on top/after SelectLock/LogicalLock.

Seems like the approach for dynamic-prune-mode can also work under static-prune-mode? Do we have a plan to merge them into one to make it easier to maintain?

For the SelectLockExec implementation's use of `tblID2PhysTblIDColIdx` it is already the same for dynamic and static prune mode. Only for UnionScan there might be a difference since UnionScan will be done per partition while SelectLock will be done per table (with a PartitionUnion for static prune mode IIRC).

Just clarifying:
The TableReader will not fill in PhysTblID/PidColID with the physical table id. For dynamic prune mode it will always be done in storage. For static prune mode it will be filled in by storage in the SelectLock case, and for UnionScan it only uses a single partition/physical table id per TableReader, so the us.table.RecordPrefix() can be used directly.
I guess the basic index merge on partitioned table is fine, the bug comes when it's used with UnionScan?
OK, ignore this... it's testing the pessimistic txn lock, rather than another bug I thought..

This assumption is fragile ... 
I remember `_tidb_rowid` also assume it to be the last? @winoros

I will rework this, so it is not requiring order of handle id, PIDCol or PhysicalTableID. Although I think trying to be consistent with the order of them is a good thing, but it should not be a requirement during reading it.

The assumption is that handle_id, pid_id and physical_table_id is last, in that order.

One of the reasons is for index reads, where the column order must be the same as it is stored, see [here](https://github.com/tikv/tikv/blob/8f4f71ea655c5ba794fd2f1780e98e6c3831bc16/components/tidb_query_executors/src/index_scan_executor.rs#L58). But since PhysicalTableID is not explicitly stored, but the already stored TableID in the key-prefix, I assume we could change the requirement to allow it anywhere.
But since it is the last column added by the planner, I think it is OK to keep this.
